name: Mariner 4
dispatch: Mariner 4 did what no machine had done: it photographed another planet. Small and spare, built to fly past Mars once and send home whatever it could in the hours it had, it carried a camera and a tape recorder across the solar system and in July 1965 returned the first close-up pictures ever taken of another world — 22 grainy frames of a cratered, moon-like surface. Those images ended a century of speculation about Martian canals and civilisations in a single afternoon, and proved a spacecraft could cross interplanetary space and bring back a planet’s face. Every camera humanity has since sent to another world descends from this one.
description: The first successful Mars flyby — July 1965. The 22 grainy black-and-white photos returned ended over a century of speculation about Martian canals and life by showing a cratered, Moon-like surface.
